keo-phao-ngay: Daytime, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle. A long column of about twenty five Viet Minh soldiers hauls a green 105mm howitzer up a red-earth track that climbs diagonally across a forested hillside. Two rope lines run from the gun back to the men's shoulders and they lean forward against them. A wooden capstan winch stands at the top of the rise with two men turning its bars, and more soldiers wait further up the track. Cut branches are laid over the gun barrel. Trees, bamboo clumps and low bushes line both sides of the track. Layered hills and a flat band of mist behind. The horizon sits high and sky fills less than a third of the frame.
piroth: Inside a French artillery command bunker at Dien Bien Phu, daytime, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle. A heavyset French colonel in a khaki uniform, his left sleeve pinned up at the empty arm, stands at a long map table and speaks to four younger French officers grouped around it. The table carries a large paper map, a field telephone, binoculars and a mug. Stacked sandbag walls, plain timber roof posts and beams, a wooden ammunition crate, a hanging bulb, a doorway at the back showing pale daylight. Even flat light throughout, no dramatic lamp glow, everything clearly readable.
long-chao: Wide view from a mountainside looking down into the Dien Bien Phu valley at midday. The valley floor is a flat patchwork of green rice paddies crossed by a pale winding river and a straight dirt airstrip, with a dozen small sandbagged French strongpoints, tents and barbed wire scattered across the middle. A few parked aircraft beside the strip. Forested ridges rise around the whole basin and fold back into two or three paler layered hill shapes with a flat white band of mist. The horizon sits high.
keo-phao-dem: Night in light blue-grey tones, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle. Rain falls in thin straight strokes. About twenty Viet Minh soldiers haul the howitzer along a narrow ledge track cut into a steep hillside. Several men carry bamboo torches whose small warm orange flames are the only warm colour in the picture; everything else is pale blue-grey and still clearly readable, never black. The track is wet red-brown mud. Bamboo and bushes on the uphill side, a drop and layered pale hills on the downhill side.
so-chi-huy: Inside a Viet Minh command dugout in the forest, daytime, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle. A Vietnamese general in a plain faded-green uniform and pith helmet leans over a paper map spread on a bamboo table with one hand flat on it. Five staff officers stand and sit around the table, two writing, one holding a field telephone. Earth walls, bamboo roof poles, a kerosene lamp, rolled maps, wooden crates, a cloth-curtained doorway with pale daylight beyond. Even flat light, everything clearly readable.
day-dut: Night in light blue-grey tones, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle looking along a steep descending track. The howitzer has broken loose and is rolling backwards down the slope, the snapped rope whipping loose in the air. Fifteen soldiers scatter to both sides with their mouths open shouting, several torches tilting as they move. One soldier is low at the base of the rear wheel, throwing himself in to wedge it. Small warm orange torch flames against the pale blue-grey night; the whole scene stays clearly readable, never black. Bushes and rocks line the track, layered pale hills behind.
ham-phao: A 105mm howitzer emplaced inside a bunker dug into a mountainside, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle from inside and to one side, so both the bunker interior and the valley through the opening are visible. Heavy timber beams and stacked sandbags frame the wide firing opening, a curtain of cut branches pulled half aside. Six Viet Minh gunners work around the gun, two carrying a shell, shells stacked in wooden racks along the earth wall. The valley outside reads as flat pale green and blue layers. Even flat light inside and out, no strong contrast between them.
phao-ban: Early evening on a forested ridge above the Dien Bien Phu valley, camera slightly elevated at a three quarter angle, the whole picture in cool blue-green twilight that is still clearly readable. Four Viet Minh artillery pieces are spaced along the ridge and fire together, each with a short flat orange muzzle flash, gun crews of three or four men around each. Below and beyond, the valley floor shows small white burst shapes and flat grey columns of smoke rising over the French positions. Layered pale hills on the far side. The horizon sits high.
